brief.topic: Open Source Text-to-Speech (TTS) Models for Language Learning Addons
brief.posting_intent: Seeking community recommendations and insights on reliable, multi-language open-source TTS models for a specific application, while also clarifying potential concerns.
brief.speaker_role: community member seeking help with explicitly hypothetical product decision, not source author
brief.current_user_goal: To find a suitable open-source TTS model for an Anki addon that generates audio for language learning flashcards, prioritizing local execution and multi-language support.
brief.current_decision: Evaluating XTTS2 as a potential candidate but uncertain about its suitability due to perceived glitches and focus on voice cloning, and seeking alternatives.
brief.desired_help: Recommendations for consistent and reliable open-source TTS models with strong multi-language support, and clarification on potential legal/ethical concerns regarding voice cloning and audio distribution for TTS models.
brief.experimental_user_scenario: A developer is building an Anki addon for language learning and needs to integrate a local, free TTS model. They are considering XTTS2 but are hesitant due to its voice cloning focus and occasional glitches. They want to know if other models are more reliable and if there are any legal issues with using voice samples for cloning or distributing generated audio.
brief.context: The user is developing an addon for Anki, an open-source flashcard software, to generate audio samples from flashcard content for language learning. The requirement is to use a local, open-source TTS model that does not rely on paid services or APIs, as existing free options are perceived to produce lower quality audio.

drafts.title: Seeking reliable, multi-language open-source TTS models for local Anki addon with voice cloning/legal concerns
drafts.body: I'm developing an Anki addon to generate audio from flashcard content for language learning, requiring a local, open-source TTS model without paid APIs. Currently, I'm evaluating XTTS2 because of its broad language support and leaderboard performance, but it sometimes feels glitchy and focuses on voice cloning. I'm concerned if this focus might introduce legal or ethical issues, especially regarding distributing voice samples for cloning. Also, asking users to provide their own 10-second voice clips seems impractical. Does anyone have experience with more stable, consistent open-source TTS models that support multiple languages well? Additionally, any insights on legal considerations around voice cloning models and what voice samples can be shared safely would be appreciated. I'm aiming for a solution that balances quality, reliability, and compliance while running fully locally for language learners.

drafts.title: Seeking reliable, multi-language open-source TTS models for a local Anki addon—concerns about XTTS2 and voice cloning legality
drafts.body: I'm developing an addon for Anki (an open-source flashcard software) to generate audio samples from flashcard content for language learning. The goal is to use a local, open-source TTS model that doesn't rely on paid services or APIs, since existing free addons don't offer good audio quality. XTTS2 is my current candidate due to its broad language support and leaderboard performance, but it sometimes feels glitchy and seems focused on voice cloning. I'm unsure if that focus raises legal or ethical issues, especially regarding which voice samples I can distribute for cloning. Also, I want to avoid requiring users to find their own voice samples, as that wouldn't be user friendly. Does anyone have experience with more consistent and reliable open-source TTS models with strong multi-language support that run locally? Additionally, any insights on potential legal concerns or best practices around voice cloning and distributing voice samples for TTS would be appreciated.

drafts.title: 为本地Anki插件寻找可靠的多语言开源TTS模型，关注语音克隆及法律问题
drafts.body: 我正在开发一个Anki插件，用于根据抽认卡内容生成语言学习音频，要求使用本地开源TTS模型，不依赖付费API。目前我在评估XTTS2，因其支持多语言且在排行榜上表现良好，但有时感觉有些“故障”，且主要聚焦于语音克隆。我担心这种聚焦可能带来法律或伦理问题，尤其是关于分发用于克隆的语音样本。此外，要求用户提供自己的10秒语音片段似乎不太实际。有人有使用更稳定、可靠且支持多语言的开源TTS模型的经验吗？另外，关于语音克隆模型的法律考虑以及哪些语音样本可以安全分享，也希望得到一些见解。我希望找到一个在质量、可靠性和合规性之间平衡，同时完全本地运行，适合语言学习者的解决方案。

drafts.title: 为本地Anki插件寻找可靠的多语言开源TTS模型——关于XTTS2及语音克隆合法性的疑虑
drafts.body: 我正在为Anki（一款开源抽认卡软件）开发一个插件，用于根据抽认卡内容生成语言学习音频样本。目标是使用本地开源TTS模型，不依赖任何付费服务或API，因为现有免费插件没有提供音质较好的选项。XTTS2是我当前的候选，因其支持多语言且在排行榜上表现良好，但有时感觉有些“故障”，且似乎专注于语音克隆。我不确定这种专注是否会引发法律或伦理问题，尤其是关于我可以分发哪些语音样本用于克隆。此外，我想避免要求用户自行寻找语音样本，因为这对用户不友好。有人有使用更稳定可靠且支持多语言的本地开源TTS模型的经验吗？另外，关于语音克隆及分发语音样本的潜在法律问题或最佳实践，也希望得到一些建议。
